context.analysis:
## Overview
[System modernizes a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims platform by gradually migrating claim types to a cloud-native Azure architecture. It ensures zero data loss and seamless hybrid coexistence during the transition.]

## Key Elements
* Policyholders and Brokers: External users submitting claims online via mobile/web UI.
* Claims Adjusters: Internal users managing claims via a high-performance web application.
* New Claims Platform: Cloud-native containerized application hosted in Azure West Europe.
* API Gateway / Integration Layer: Hybrid routing and abstraction barrier managing legacy decoupling.
* Legacy Mainframe: On-premises COBOL/DB2 system remaining the system of record.
* Insurer Active Directory / Microsoft Entra ID: Identity provider managing authentication and SSO.

## Relationships
* Policyholders, Brokers, and Adjusters interact with the New Claims Platform via HTTPS.
* New Claims Platform communicates with the API Gateway using REST over HTTPS.
* API Gateway interfaces with the Legacy Mainframe using native TCP/SNA/DB2 protocols via mTLS.
* New Claims Platform integrates with Microsoft Entra ID using OIDC/OAuth2 for federated single sign-on.

## Technology Stack
* Cloud Platform: Microsoft Azure (West Europe) chosen for enterprise hosting.
* Integration & Routing: API Gateway enforcing rate limiting, mTLS, and Strangler Fig routing.
* Infrastructure as Code: Terraform or Bicep to mitigate low team cloud experience.
* Security & IAM: Microsoft Entra ID with OAuth2/OIDC and AES-256/TLS 1.3 encryption.
* Observability: Azure Application Insights and Azure Sentinel for distributed tracing and SIEM.

## Rationale
[The hybrid architecture utilizes a Strangler Fig pattern behind an API Gateway to isolate the rigid legacy mainframe from frequent changes. This design satisfies strict performance, security, and one-day rollback requirements while mitigating risks associated with the team's low cloud experience.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
This hybrid cloud architecture incrementally modernizes a legacy insurance claims platform by migrating claim types one by one to Azure. It maintains the 30-year-old on-premise mainframe as the system of record while using an asynchronous, event-driven integration layer to ensure zero data loss and enable rapid rollbacks.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Policyholders, Brokers, and Claims Adjusters
- **External Systems**: Microsoft Entra ID (SSO), API Gateway / On-Premise Mainframe (COBOL/DB2)
- **Customer Portal**: React SPA hosted in Azure Static Web Apps
- **Adjuster Web Application**: Node.js/ASP.NET Core BFF paired with a PostgreSQL read-cache
- **Claims Processing Service**: .NET Core microservices handling core domain logic
- **Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL)**: Integration service translating modern events to legacy formats
- **Migration Operations Dashboard**: React SPA and .NET Core API for business reconciliation
- **Messaging & Infrastructure**: Azure Service Bus, Azure Container Apps (ACA), and Azure Key Vault

## Relationships
- **Customers/Brokers -> Customer Portal**: HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
- **Adjusters -> Adjuster Web App**: HTTPS (TLS 1.3) with OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 via Microsoft Entra ID
- **Adjuster Web App -> PostgreSQL**: TCP / TLS for low-latency read caching
- **Claims Processing Service <-> Azure Service Bus**: AMQP / HTTPS for asynchronous messaging
- **ACL <-> API Gateway / Mainframe**: gRPC over mTLS and secure IP whitelisting
- **Containers -> Azure Key Vault**: Managed Identities with HTTPS for dynamic secret injection

## Technology Stack
- **Azure Container Apps (ACA)**: Abstracts Kubernetes complexity for a team with low cloud experience
- **.NET Core & Node.js**: Powers microservices and Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) applications
- **PostgreSQL**: Delivers sub-2s read-model caching to decouple from mainframe latency
- **Azure Service Bus**: Ensures reliable messaging, circuit breaking, and dead-letter queueing during mainframe batch windows
- **Microsoft Entra ID**: Enforces Single Sign-On (SSO) and RBAC/ABAC security controls
- **Bicep / Terraform**: Automates infrastructure-as-code deployment with pre-configured Azure Monitor / Application Insights

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture protects the business by keeping the stable legacy mainframe as the system of record while isolating changes via an Anti-Corruption Layer. Using managed Azure services minimizes operational overhead for an inexperienced cloud team while meeting strict sub-2s performance and one-day rollback requirements.

Customer Portal.analysis:
## Overview
Modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurer mainframe claims system by gradually migrating claim types to a hybrid cloud architecture. The new platform enables online claim submissions and adjuster workflows while ensuring data consistency and strict security.

## Key Elements
- Policyholders and Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Customer Portal (React SPA)
- Adjuster Web Application (Node.js / ASP.NET Core BFF)
- Claims Processing Service (.NET Core microservices)
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL)
- PostgreSQL Read-Cache
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2)
- Microsoft Entra ID / Active Directory

## Relationships
- Policyholders and Brokers -> Customer Portal: Accesses portal for claims [HTTPS (TLS 1.3)]
- Customer Portal -> API Gateway / Integration Layer: Submits and tracks claims [HTTPS/REST]
- Claims Processing Service -> Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL): Translates modern and legacy schemas [Internal Messaging]
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) -> Legacy Mainframe: Synchronizes records [SNA / Batch Protocols]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Static Web Apps: Hosts frontend React SPA with native CDN
- React & MSAL.js: Powers UI components and OIDC/OAuth2 authentication
- PostgreSQL: Provides low-latency read-cache for adjuster screens (<2s requirement)
- .NET Core: Implements claims processing microservices
- Azure Service Bus: Handles asynchronous messaging between services

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture allows incremental migration of claim types without destabilizing the legacy mainframe system of record. Decoupling the new web frontend via an Anti-Corruption Layer ensures sub-second performance while maintaining strict data consistency.

- Adjuster Web Application -> Azure Service Bus: Dispatches asynchronous commands [AMQP / TLS]
- Adjuster Web Application -> Microsoft Entra ID: Authenticates users and exchanges tokens [HTTPS / OIDC]

## Rationale
- Standardizing on .NET Core reduces cognitive load and tech-stack fragmentation for teams with limited cloud experience.
- Decoupling the UI via a PostgreSQL read-cache ensures high performance while insulating adjusters from legacy mainframe latency.

PostgreSQL Read-Cache.analysis:
## Overview
The architecture implements a hybrid insurance claims platform using Azure Database for PostgreSQL to cache mainframe data for modern adjusters. It ensures sub-2-second response times while maintaining data synchronization during the three-year legacy migration.

## Key Elements
- Cache Storage Engine (Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server)
- Sync Consumer Component (.NET worker hosted in Azure Container Apps)
- Audit & Versioning Manager (.NET Library / Service Layer)
- Azure Service Bus
- Azure Key Vault
- Adjuster Web Application

## Relationships
- Adjuster Web Application -> Cache Storage Engine: Queries claim read-models [PostgreSQL Protocol / TLS 1.3]
- Anti-Corruption Layer / Azure Service Bus -> Sync Consumer Component: Ingests delta change events [AMQP]
- Sync Consumer Component -> Cache Storage Engine: Writes updates via connection pooling [TCP / TLS 1.3]
- Cache Storage Engine -> Azure Key Vault: Retrieves Customer-Managed Keys for TDE [HTTPS / REST]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server: Managed database instance to reduce stateful cloud operations overhead
- .NET / Azure Container Apps: Scalable worker hosting for asynchronous event consumption
- Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous messaging broker for handling change data feeds
- Microsoft Entra ID & Azure RBAC: Enforces secretless authentication and least-privilege database roles

## Rationale
Managed Azure services minimize operational complexity for a cloud-inexperienced team while meeting strict security standards. Decomposing the read-cache into isolated read, write, and audit components guarantees sub-2-second UI performance and data freshness without risking the legacy mainframe.

Claims Processing Service.analysis:
## Overview
Gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe claims system with a modern Azure-hosted platform while maintaining legacy processing. The system ensures zero data loss and enables continuous operations during a three-year hybrid migration.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Policyholders, Brokers, and Claims Adjusters
- **External Systems**: API Gateway, Legacy Mainframe, Microsoft Entra ID
- **Containers**: Customer Portal (React SPA in Azure Static Web Apps), Adjuster Web Application (Node.js/ASP.NET Core BFF), PostgreSQL Read-Cache, Claims Processing Service (.NET Core microservices), Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL), Migration Operations Dashboard, Azure Service Bus, Azure Container Apps, Azure Key Vault
- **Components (Claims Processing Service)**: Claim Orchestrator Component, Claim Domain Model Component, Exception Handler Component, Integration Client Component

## Relationships
- Customer Portal & Adjuster Web Application -> API Gateway: Secure HTTPS requests
- API Gateway -> Claims Processing Service: mTLS and JWT validation via Microsoft Entra ID [HTTPS]
- Claims Processing Service -> Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous messaging [AMQP / TLS 1.3]
- Claims Processing Service -> Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL): Resilient communication with circuit breakers [HTTPS / Polly]
- Anti-Corruption Layer -> Legacy Mainframe: Synchronized legacy database updates [DB2 / SNA]

## Technology Stack
- **Compute**: Azure Container Apps (hosting .NET Core microservices and Node.js BFF)
- **Database**: PostgreSQL (handling read-cache and persistent state)
- **Messaging**: Azure Service Bus (managing asynchronous domain events and dead-letter queues)
- **Security & Secrets**: Microsoft Entra ID (SSO/JWT) and Azure Key Vault with Managed Identities (CMK encryption)
- **Resilience & Tracing**: Polly (.NET circuit breakers) and OpenTelemetry (distributed tracing)

## Rationale
The hybrid container architecture isolates the fragile legacy mainframe using an Anti-Corruption Layer and circuit breakers, ensuring sub-2-second adjuster response times. Lean .NET Core microservices deployed in Azure match the team's cloud skillset while meeting strict consistency and rollback requirements.

Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL).analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid cloud insurance claims modernization platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe. Its core purpose is to process and migrate claims safely while maintaining continuity with the legacy system.

## Key Elements
*   Policyholders and Brokers
*   Claims Adjusters
*   Migration Operations Team
*   Customer Portal (React SPA in Azure Static Web Apps)
*   Adjuster Web Application (Node.js / ASP.NET Core BFF)
*   Claims Processing Service (.NET Core microservices)
*   Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) (Azure Container Apps)
*   Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2 on-premise)
*   Microsoft Entra ID and Azure Key Vault

## Relationships
*   Customer Portal -> Claims Processing Service via HTTPS/REST
*   Adjuster Web Application -> Claims Processing Service via HTTPS/REST
*   Claims Processing Service -> Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) via Azure Service Bus
*   Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) -> Legacy Mainframe via gRPC over mTLS
*   Migration Operations Dashboard -> ACL Replay Coordinator via REST over HTTPS with Entra ID JWT validation

## Technology Stack
*   **Frontend:** React SPA for user portals and operations dashboards
*   **Backend:** .NET Core microservices and Node.js/ASP.NET Core for modern services
*   **Integration:** Azure Container Apps hosted Anti-Corruption Layer with JSON-to-COBOL mapping
*   **Security:** Microsoft Entra ID for SSO/RBAC and Azure Key Vault for mTLS secrets
*   **Infrastructure:** Hybrid deployment across on-premise mainframe and Azure West Europe

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe changes while using Azure cloud services for modern web applications. The Anti-Corruption Layer ensures zero data loss and enables rapid one-day rollbacks per claim type.

    name: "Service Bus Message Listener"
    technology: ".NET Core / Azure Service Bus SDK"
    description: "Listens for claim migration and processing events from the Azure Service Bus."
  - type: "component"
    name: "JSON-to-COBOL Mapper"
    technology: ".NET Core Library"
    description: "Translates modern JSON payloads into mainframe-compatible COBOL structures."
  - type: "component"
    name: "Replay Coordinator"
    technology: ".NET Core API Controller"
    description: "Manages claim replays and coordinates with the Migration Operations Dashboard via REST over HTTPS with Entra ID JWT validation."
  - type: "component"

Migration Operations Dashboard.analysis:
## Overview
[The Migration Operations Dashboard provides real-time visibility, reconciliation alerts, and kill-switch controls to safely manage the multi-year transition from the legacy mainframe to the modern platform.]

## Key Elements
- Dashboard UI (React SPA)
- Dashboard API Controller (.NET Core Web API)
- Reconciliation Engine (.NET Core Component)
- Kill-Switch Orchestrator (.NET Core Component)
- Reconciliation Report Generator (.NET Core Component)
- Discrepancy Translation Service (.NET Core Component)

## Relationships
- Dashboard UI interacts with Dashboard API Controller via HTTPS/REST and SignalR
- Dashboard API Controller invokes Reconciliation Engine via MediatR domain events
- Reconciliation Engine queries PostgreSQL Read-Cache via EF Core and Legacy Mainframe via Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL)
- Kill-Switch Orchestrator publishes domain events to Azure Service Bus
- Reconciliation Report Generator stores/retrieves files in Azure Blob Storage

## Technology Stack
- React SPA: Chosen for modern UI capabilities while aligning with the team's skillset
- .NET Core: Selected for robust backend microservices and API controllers
- Azure Service Bus: Used for reliable asynchronous operational command dispatch
- Azure Blob Storage: Implemented for scalable asynchronous export file storage
- Microsoft Entra ID: Enforces strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

## Rationale
- This architecture fits requirements by isolating complex migration logic into dedicated components while enforcing strict security, operational guardrails, and rapid 24-hour rollback capabilities.

Messaging & Infrastructure.analysis:
## Overview
• The system is a hybrid cloud messaging and infrastructure layer designed to support the gradual modernization of a 30-year-old mainframe claims platform.
• It provides reliable asynchronous messaging, secure secret management, container orchestration, and immutable auditing to ensure zero claim loss during migration.

## Key Elements
• Message Broker Interface: Azure Service Bus with AMQP 1.0 and Dead-Letter Queues.
• Container Runtime Host: Azure Container Apps with KEDA for microservices orchestration.
• Secret & Config Store: Azure Key Vault for credentials and connection strings.
• Audit & Telemetry Forwarder: Azure Monitor and OpenTelemetry exporter.
• Storage Sink: Azure Blob Storage with WORM policies for immutable audit logs.

## Relationships
• Claims Processing Service -> Message Broker Interface: Publishes and consumes claim events [AMQP 1.0].
• Container Runtime Host -> Audit & Telemetry Forwarder: Emits traces and audit logs [HTTPS].
• Azure Container Apps -> Azure Service Bus & Azure Key Vault: Authenticates via Microsoft Entra ID Managed Identities [mTLS / Private Endpoints].

## Technology Stack
• Azure Service Bus: Chosen for managed, reliable asynchronous messaging to prevent data loss (R-04).
• Azure Container Apps & KEDA: Selected to provide event-driven scaling while mitigating the team's lack of deep Kubernetes experience.
• Azure Key Vault: Implemented for centralized secret management and automated 90-day secret rotation.
• Azure Blob Storage WORM: Utilized for immutable audit logging to satisfy insurance compliance standards.
• Azure Bicep & GitHub Actions: Deployed via Infrastructure as Code with automated smoke tests for zero-downtime blue-green deployments.

## Rationale
• This architecture directly satisfies zero-loss consistency (R-04) and maintainability (R-06) requirements through reliable managed queuing and clear component boundaries.
• It minimizes operational overhead for a cloud-inexperienced team while meeting strict hybrid-cloud security and regulatory compliance constraints.
